page.title: Contact Sheet
page.purpose: Render a grid across two chosen axes so a style family is evaluated as a set. This is the surface that makes the taxonomy tangible — the axes stop being a schema and become a space you can look at.

priorities.statement: The cost of a sweep is stated before it runs.
priorities.notes: A sweep is N renders. A procedural sweep is free; a model-backed sweep is N times the unit cost. The operator sees which, and the cell count, before starting.

priorities.statement: Skipped cells are reported, never silently dropped.
priorities.notes: A partial grid presented as complete is a lie about coverage. Each skipped cell names why — an unsatisfiable axis combination, a licence block, or a failed render.

priorities.statement: The grid is readable as a comparison, with axes labelled on both edges.
priorities.notes: The point is seeing what changes along each axis, which requires the axis to be legible without counting tiles.

states.description: Sweep rows reserve their grid geometry while candidates render.
The last sweep remains visible with a freshness notice.
Sweep failure names the failed operation and offers retry.
No sweep axes are selected and the operator is prompted to configure them.
Two axes chosen, cell count and estimated cost shown, run available.
Cells populate progressively; the grid holds its shape so it does not reflow as results arrive.
Every cell rendered, each showing its verdict, with any cell promotable to a full candidate review.
Some cells were skipped. The grid shows which and why, and the summary states the coverage achieved rather than implying completeness.
The configured sweep exceeds the available metered allowance. States the allowance, the required amount, and offers a procedural-only sweep as an alternative.
